name: OpenCode
summary: An open-source (MIT) coding agent that works with 75+ model providers and local models, built as a local server with a terminal interface as one of its clients.
intro: OpenCode runs in the terminal, as a desktop app or inside an editor. It isn’t tied to one model vendor: it uses the AI SDK and the Models.dev catalogue to reach more than 75 providers, plus models running locally. Two built-in agents switch with the Tab key: `build`, the default, with full access, and `plan`, which is read-only, denies file edits and asks before running shell commands. A `general` subagent handles searches and multi-step side tasks. It can start language servers for the files it touches and feed their diagnostics back to the model.

Under the interface is a client/server split. Starting `opencode` starts both a TUI and an HTTP server, and `opencode serve` runs the server alone, with an OpenAPI 3.1 spec at `/doc` that is also used to generate an SDK. IDE plugins drive the TUI through that server, and `opencode acp` speaks the Agent Client Protocol for editors that support it.

Instructions come from `AGENTS.md` (created by `/init`), found by walking up from the current directory, then a global `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`. For people moving from Claude Code it also reads `CLAUDE.md` and `~/.claude/skills` unless told not to. Permissions resolve each action to allow, ask or deny, and start permissive: most actions are allowed, while touching paths outside the project and a tool call repeated three times with identical input (`doom_loop`) ask first, and `.env` files can’t be read.
strengths: Provider-agnostic: swap between hosted models, existing subscriptions and local models without changing tools
MIT-licensed, with a documented HTTP API, so you can script it or build your own client
Reads `CLAUDE.md` and Claude Code skills, which makes switching cheap
Language-server diagnostics give the model compiler-grade feedback after each edit
limits: Permissive defaults: most actions run without asking unless you add `ask` or `deny` rules
Results depend on the model you pick; there is no single vendor tuning model and harness together
The server is unsecured unless you set `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`, so be careful binding it beyond `127.0.0.1`
Easy to confuse with the archived Go project `opencode-ai/opencode`, which now continues as Crush under Charm

snippet.title: Run it in a terminal, one-shot, or as a server
source: curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash   # or: npm i -g opencode-ai
opencode                         # TUI; Tab switches between the build and plan agents
opencode run "explain how the auth middleware works"   # one message, then exit
# headless server: the same API the TUI and IDE plugins use

story: OpenCode’s repository started in spring 2025 under the GitHub organisation of SST, and published its first releases in May 2025. Until June its README described a Go program with a Bubble Tea terminal interface and promised “a complete overhaul” for mid-June; the rewrite that followed is written in TypeScript. Another Go project called OpenCode, `opencode-ai/opencode`, has been archived and continues as Crush, developed by its original author and the Charm team; OpenCode’s own FAQ says that repository has no relation to it.

Its FAQ set out the pitch against Claude Code: similar capability, but fully open source, not coupled to any provider (Anthropic was recommended, but OpenAI, Google and local models work too), language-server support out of the box, a terminal interface built by Neovim users and the creators of terminal.shop, and a client/server design so the TUI is just one possible client. Version 1.0.0 shipped on 31 October 2025. By February 2026 the repository had over 95,000 stars, and it now lives under Anomaly’s GitHub organisation.

choices.why: Its authors expected the gaps between models to close and prices to drop, so being able to switch providers mattered more than tuning for one.

choices.choice: A server first, the TUI as a client
choices.why: Separating the agent from its interface lets it run on one machine while being driven from another, such as a phone, and lets IDE plugins and scripts use the same API.
Diagnostics from a language server tell the model about type errors right after an edit, without waiting for a build or test run.
Reading `CLAUDE.md` and Claude Code skills by default lowers the cost of trying it in a repository already set up for another agent.

timeline.text: First releases under SST’s GitHub organisation (May)
The Go version is replaced by a rewrite announced for mid-June
Passes 95,000 GitHub stars; published by Anomaly Innovations
